DEINE MISSION

Die Energiekosten in Europa sind doppelt so hoch wie in den USA und China. Gleichzeitig wird sich die Stromnachfrage bis 2050 voraussichtlich verdoppeln. Marktpreisvolatilität und zunehmende Komplexität werden uns erhalten bleiben. Damit steht das Rückgrat der europäischen Industrie unter Druck - und Unternehmen müssen jetzt handeln.

trawa entwickelt die Lösung: die erste integrierte B2B-Energieplattform, die Energiebeschaffung, Energiemanagement und die Steuerung von Flexibilitäten in einem Produkt vereint. Diese Integration ermöglicht Einsparungen von bis zu 30 % bei den wiederkehrenden Stromkosten und unterstützt Unternehmen gleichzeitig dabei, auf erneuerbare Energien umzusteigen.

Wir sind Europas am schnellsten wachsende B2B-Energieplattform. Aktuell sind wir in Deutschland und Österreich aktiv und planen, unsere Aktivitäten 2027 auf einen dritten Markt auszuweiten. Die Position ist in Berlin angesiedelt. trawa ist ein Office-First-Unternehmen: In der Regel arbeitest du an fünf Tagen pro Woche aus unserem Büro.

Unser Revenue Operations Team ist ein zentraler Wachstumstreiber für den kommerziellen Erfolg von trawa. Es verbindet verschiedene Teams, schafft effiziente Prozesse und befähigt unseren Vertrieb, sein volles Potenzial zu entfalten. Dadurch entsteht ein dynamisches Umfeld, das nachhaltiges Wachstum ermöglicht. Nach einer Phase starken Wachstums gilt es nun, das Team gezielt für die nächste Wachstumsphase aufzustellen - sowohl für die weitere Skalierung in unserem Heimatmarkt Deutschland als auch für die Expansion in weitere Märkte.

title: Product Manager (FTC)
description:
Product Manager, Prolific For Research ( UK Remote)

(6 Month Fixed Term Contract or Contractor Engagement)

Team: Product 

Prolific

Prolific is not just another player in the AI space - we are the architects of the human data infrastructure that's reshaping the landscape of AI development. In a world where foundational AI technologies are increasingly commoditised, it's the quality and diversity of human-generated data that truly differentiates products and models.

The Role

Prolific for Research helps researchers reach the right participants for their study and run more sophisticated, higher-value research. That includes work on helping researchers find exactly who they need for a study, and on supporting research studies that are more complex in scope or duration than a single one-off survey.

We're looking for a Product Manager to take ownership of the next phase of the Research roadmap, scaling what's already shipped, growing adoption, and iterating based on researcher feedback. The nature of the projects/work that this role will cover, means that the role can be offered as either a fixed-term employee or contractor  basis.

Impact: You'll own the outcomes of a small, stream-aligned team within our Research Group. Online research is changing fast amid AI-tools that are re-shaping the playing field and raising the expectations and challenges of providing trustworthy samples.

Experience: You'll bring a track record of shipping and scaling products that simplify complex workflows for demanding professional or enterprise users, and know how to use data and user behaviour to inform decisions. Experience building for researchers or research tools is a plus, but we're just as interested in strong product fundamentals from elsewhere.

Domain: This is core to Prolific's 2026 strategy, and to how we deepen our value for research customers ranging from individual academics to institutional and enterprise accounts.

Responsibilities: You'll product manage a small team of engineers, hands-on with discovery and delivery, and accountable for delivering key outcomes. You'll work closely with fellow Product Managers across Research and AI, the VP of Research, and collaborators across human data operations, integrity, support, science, sales, and client services.

Culture: Adding on to our Prolific Principles, we expect colleagues in the Product, Research, and Design Group to demonstrate reliability, grit, diplomacy, a bias for action, and a dogged focus on value - you'll be a champion of these behaviours yourself, and in the culture of your team. Accountability and autonomy are two sides of the same coin, and we expect you to demonstrate both.

What you'll be doing

• Help researchers find exactly the participants they need for a study, beyond broad demographic targeting.

• Grow adoption of more ambitious study designs, such as research that runs longer or asks more of participants than a single one-off survey.

• Own the supporting tools that make these more advanced study types easier to run.

• Run the day-to-day product lifecycle for your areas: prioritisation, delivery, measurement, and iteration.

• Be an unblocker and simplifier of complexity: colleagues will bring you problems, and emerge optimistic, with solutions.

• Partner closely with Engineering and Design as a tight product trio, in a test-learn-iterate fashion.

What you’ll bring

• A track record working embedded in technology teams alongside engineers and designers.

• A builder mindset and experience with AI tools and workflows for PMs.

• Experience shipping for demanding professional or enterprise users, research, survey, or data-collection tools, or complex B2B workflows, are all relevant.

• Fluency in modern Product/Engineering practice: Agile, continuous discovery and delivery, JTBD, vertical slicing, test-learn-iterate.

• Strong commercial acumen and data-informed decision-making, paired with a storyteller's flair and a relentless can-do attitude.

Our client is a boutique consulting firm that employs consultants and professionals with unique skill sets to support the federal government with strategic execution, financial process enablement, IT systems, and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software implementation.

• Design the accounting derivation path from project, task, and expenditure attributes into the Department's multi-segment account classification code structure, in partnership with the Functional Lead and Financial Specialist.

• Own the technical path through the Department's Jira and Bitbucket release workflow, including version control, peer review, build traceability, configuration management, rollback packaging, and post-implementation review evidence.

• Lead technical impact analysis and risk-based regression design to protect existing FMSS interfaces and period-close processing.

• Produce configuration screenshots, architecture and data-flow artifacts, and technical evidence supporting the major system change compliance process.

• Lead the technical execution of production deployment, including configuration and data migration from test environments

Are you the person on your team who builds the agent everyone else ends up using? We're looking for an AI Engineer to join our Training Product team and do that at Baseten. You'll build AI-driven product features for the customers training and post-training frontier models on our platform, and you'll raise the ceiling on how Baseten itself uses AI internally, turning manual workflows into agentic ones that make every other team faster.

You'll work directly with our research engineers to scope and build products, taking ideas from a research loop that already works internally to something customers can run themselves. This is a hands-on role with real autonomy. You'll pick the problems worth solving, build the harnesses, execution flows, and guardrails that make AI systems reliable, and own the results. If you've been shipping agents and want that to be the job, let's talk.

- Build and ship agentic product experiences, including chat-style and assistant-like interfaces, from prototype to GA.

- Design the harnesses, execution flows, and guardrails that make AI systems reliable in production.

- Build internal automation and AI tooling that measurably increases the velocity of engineering, research, and go-to-market teams.

- Partner with research engineers to scope product opportunities out of internal research workflows and turn them into customer-facing features.

- Define and instrument evals so you know whether a change actually improved output quality.

- Work throughout the stack (API layer, backend, agent orchestration, frontend) to implement features end to end.

- Use Baseten's own training and inference products yourself to develop intuition around customer workflows.

- Identify where AI can replace manual process across the company and build the thing rather than write the proposal.

- Fix bugs and resolve customer issues with urgency.

title: Social Media Coordinator
description:
About Bask & Lather Co.
Bask & Lather Co. is a fast-growing, family-founded haircare brand dedicated to restoring
crowns and confidence. What began as a kitchen remedy has grown into one of the most
recognized textured-hair brands in the United States, known for transformative products,
authentic storytelling, and a deeply engaged community.

As we continue to grow, social media plays a critical role in how customers discover,
experience, and connect with Bask & Lather. We are building a social team that moves quickly,
understands culture, creates consistently, and produces content that earns attention and drives
action.

The Opportunity
Bask & Lather is seeking a creative, resourceful, and highly organized Social Media Coordinator
to support the daily execution of our organic social media and content strategy.

This is a hands-on content-creation role. A primary responsibility of the Social Media
Coordinator is to regularly film, edit, publish, and appear in original social content. This is not
simply a scheduling, community-management, or administrative position.

The successful candidate must be comfortable picking up a phone or camera, setting up lighting
and audio, directing talent, capturing multiple concepts, and editing footage into polished,
platform-native content. This person will create content from products, employees, customer
stories, office moments, retail activations, trends, launches, and cultural conversations.

The ideal candidate is deeply familiar with social culture, moves with urgency, accepts creative
feedback well, and enjoys working both behind and in front of the camera.

Key Responsibilities

Content Filming and Production
● Regularly film original social content at Bask & Lather’s office, content studios, retail
locations, brand events, activations, and other approved locations.

● Capture short-form videos, product demonstrations, tutorials, transformations, founder
and employee content, customer stories, educational content, behind-the-scenes
moments, and trend-based concepts.
● Film using smartphones, cameras, lighting, microphones, tripods, and other production
equipment.
● Prepare filming environments and ensure appropriate lighting, framing, sound, styling,
products, props, talent, and backgrounds.
● Direct employees, models, creators, customers, and other participants during content
capture.
● Comfortably appear on camera, demonstrate products, provide voiceovers, participate in
trends, and host social content when needed.
● Edit short-form videos using CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, native platform tools, or
similar software.
● Create and edit graphics, static posts, carousels, Stories, Reels, short-form videos, and
other platform-native content.
● Add captions, graphics, sound, transitions, hooks, calls to action, and other creative
elements that improve content performance.
● Repurpose footage into multiple versions, formats, hooks, and platform-specific edits.
● Organize raw footage, edited content, project files, and approved assets within the
company’s content library.

expectations.

opportunities.

Social Media Execution

strengthen Bask & Lather’s online identity.

content strategy.

moments into platform-native content.

We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~110 people, more than half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle

The Opportunity

You will report to the Site Manager/Head of Site and will run shifts at one of our Hybrid Sort Centres (HSCs), leading 50-100+ operatives through high-volume, time-pressured sortation where minutes matter and small deviations cascade into missed deadlines. Each of our HSCs handle over 40 million parcels annually, with our largest site measuring more than 300,000 sq ft.

You will also be accountable for whether the site is measurably better in a month than it is today for each of our key metrics. You are on the floor for your shift, every shift. This is not a project role with occasional site visits and it is not a desk job, the forward work happens along with running the operation.

 

Who will thrive in this role

- Deliver shift plan end to end people deployment, throughput, quality standards, and health & safety compliance

- Lead, develop, and performance-manage a frontline team of 50-100+ operatives

- Own the end-of-shift handover; what happened, what is at risk, what the next shift needs to know

- Stay decisive through volume peaks, outages, and labour gaps. Triage, solve the problem at hand quickly, contain the impact, restore flow

- Present and write clearly whether briefs, escalations, handovers or post-incident reviews. Decisions here get made based off what you wrote

- Implement changes into a live operation such as introducing robotics, launching new sortation tech or onboarding new clients. We are changing the operations constantly which means you’ll roll change out mid flight and bring your team along the journey.

 

Who you are

- Scaled something from zero: a site, a market, a process or a program.

- Managed a physical operation: quick commerce, grocery, e-commerce fulfillment, last mile, 3PL, food production, airport ground handling, rail. Anywhere with a hard cut off and people on the floor.

- Communicate in both directions and have strong people management skills: you can brief 80 operatives at shift start and take a problem to senior leadership the same day.

- Built a mechanism that held: a control, a cadence, a metric, a document standard. Something you authored that changed how frontline teams worked.

- Own numbers rather than report them: you can name a metric you created or redefined, explain why the previous one was wrong, and say what changed afterwards.

- Understand frontline work: one of these must be true: you have personally led frontline teams; you have worked embedded in and around a frontline population day to day, without the reporting line; or you have been accountable for outcomes delivered by frontline people you did not employ.

Resource Generation: Analyzing task quality trends and autonomously developing educational resources and feedback documentation to increase alignment between AI task outputs and campaign expectations.

title: Digital Experience & Website Lead – 12 month FTC
description:
What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business - where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent - it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

Does this sound like you?
Flagstone is entering a pivotal phase for its website - a full redesign and relaunch, running alongside a parallel Brand refresh. We're looking for a senior website and digital experience leader to own this as a strategic programme, and to lead our cross-functional Website team (product, UX, data, engineering, and digital marketing).

This is not a day-to-day execution role. You'll set the direction and commercial strategy for the site, sequence the programme, and coordinate contributors across Brand, Marketing, Growth/Creative, Data, and Tech - while giving your team the space to execute against a clear plan. You've owned a public website as a commercial and brand-critical asset before, and you'll need minimal supervision on process: you're trusted to run the show, escalating only what genuinely needs senior leadership's input rather than day-to-day noise.

You might currently hold a title such as Head of Website, Head of Web Experience, Head of Conversion Rate Optimisation, or Digital Product Marketing Lead. What matters isn't whether you've been called a "Product Manager" - it's that you've owned a website end-to-end as a revenue and brand-driving channel, and know how to run CRO, experimentation, and digital experience at scale.

What you’ll do:
Own the strategy and roadmap for the website redesign and relaunch, working hand-in-hand with the Brand team so the two workstreams land as one coherent outcome

- Act as squad lead for the Website squad - setting priorities, unblocking the team, and holding the cross-functional group (product, UX, data, engineering, digital marketing) to a shared plan

- Design and run the end-to-end programme of work: sequencing dependencies across product, marketing, creative, data, and engineering, and keeping it on track without needing to escalate routine issues upward

- Define the strategic direction for site structure, customer journeys, and conversion approach, translating business goals into a clear plan the squad can execute against

- Represent the website programme to senior stakeholders - bringing clarity and options, not problems, to conversations with the Senior Leadership Team

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today - and we’re just getting started.

ROLE OVERVIEW

As an Enterprise Account Executive on Harvey's State & Local team, you will own a multi-state territory of state Attorneys General offices, state agencies, judiciaries, and large county and municipal legal departments. These are substantial legal organizations - a single state AG office can run to hundreds of attorneys - and almost none of them are using AI today. Compared with federal, the territory is broader and higher-velocity: more accounts, more procurement variation across jurisdictions, and paths to direct purchase that can move faster than the federal cycle. You will run the full cycle and help define how Harvey sells to government at the state level.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own a named multi-state territory of AG offices, state agencies, judiciaries, and large local government legal departments, running the full cycle from prospecting through contracting and expansion.

- Achieve and exceed revenue targets while managing a higher account volume than a federal book.

- Map the procurement path per jurisdiction - competitive solicitation, state tender panels, cooperative purchasing vehicles, or direct purchase under a legal services or professional services exemption.

- Multi-thread across Attorneys General and deputies, general counsel, division heads, state CIO and CISO organizations, and procurement officers.

- Work against state fiscal calendars and legislative budget cycles, which vary by jurisdiction.

- Build reference strength deliberately - state government buys heavily on peer proof, so early wins must be turned into referenceable stories.

- Document learnings into a repeatable state and local playbook.

WHAT YOU HAVE

- 5+ years selling complex enterprise software, with a meaningful portion of that time carrying a state, local, or education quota.

- Closed SLED deals yourself, and can speak specifically to how you got them through procurement.

- Comfort operating across multiple jurisdictions with genuinely different procurement rules, rather than treating SLED as one market.

- Ability to manage a broader book with more concurrent cycles and a lower average deal size than federal.

- Strong detail discipline around solicitations, deadlines, and security documentation.

- Genuinely excited to prospect, and capable of independently running a cycle end to end.

- Strong consultative, value-based selling instincts, and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

- Demonstrated interest in AI and in helping government lawyers do their work better.

$400,000 USD
